FREQUENCY SHIFT KEYING (FSK)
w Describe the characteristics of FSK signals.
w Describe a typical FSK demodulator circuit.
w Describe the NE565 and NE567 PLL integrated circuits.........
OBJECTIVES
w Describe a typical FSK modulator circuit.
w Describe the MC14066 analog switch and ICL8038 VCO integrated circuits.
EQUIPMENT REQUIRED
In this lesson, you are taught another method of digital signal processing and the circuits that modulate and demodulate.
INTRODUCTIONM
The method is called Frequency Shift Keying, FSK for short.
The name FSK is from how the method originally was produced, the keying (turning on and off) of a transmitter for the telegraph and teletype.
In fact, FSK was developed long before digital circuits existed.
Telegraph and teletype signals consisted of "MARKs" and "SPACEs", which are similar to HIGHs and LOWs in digital circuits.
The MARKs and SPACEs were then used to frequency modulator (FM) with an analog carrier signal.
Then in the demodulator, the FM signal was changed back into MARKs and SPACEs.
Today, the concept of FSK is the same......................
Except that MARKs and SPACEs are replaced with HIGHs and LOWs, and the vacuum tube discrete circuits are replaced with integrated digital circuits.
Even though FSK is an old method of signal processing, it is still widely used in the military, commercial news services, and computer MODEMS. If it works, don't fix it!
Let's begin the lesson on FREQUENCY SHIFT KEYING (FSK)....................
LESSON MENU
Frequency Shift Keying is a signal processing technique that uses a digital signal to frequency modulate an analog carrier signal.
DISCUSSION
The digital information signal can be any type.
Straight digital, PCM, or DM signals can be used. This includes any synchronization, start, or stop pulses.
No matter what type of digital information is used, the signals are either HIGH or LOW.
Thus, the FM signal that is developed only has two frequency variations.
One frequency change above the FM signal represents a HIGH and another frequency change below the FM signal represent a low.
And note that the system is digital even though the carrier signal is analog.
What method of signal processing is similar to FSK?
AM is amplitude modulation. An information signal changes the amplitude of a carrier signal. FSK does not operate in this manner.
TRY AGAIN!
PCM is pulse code modulation. A digital pulse train is developed from the information signal. FSK does not operate in this manner.
TRY AGAIN!
As stated, the FSK signal is a frequency modulated signal..
And because the information signal is digital, the FSK signal contains only three frequencies.
One frequency is the center frequency, or fc.
It is generated when no information signal is used. Not shown in the FSK signal.
The second frequency, fmax, is above fc.
It is normally generated when the information signal is a "1" or a HIGH level.
Note that a "0" or LOW information signal could produce the higher frequency, it depends on the system.
It is normally generated when the information signal is "0" or a LOW level.
Note that a "1" or HIGH information signal could produce the lower frequency, it depends on the system.
What type of information signal produces fc in a FSK system?
An information signal frequency modulates the carrier signal. Normally, the HIGH information signal increases fc.
TRY AGAIN!
An information signal frequency modulates the carrier signal. Normally, the LOW information signal decreases fc.
TRY AGAIN!
Although FSK is similar to FM, it does have one difference.
Recall that FM changes the carrier signal FREQUENCY in accordance with the AMPLITUDE of the information signal.
The greater the amplitude level, the greater the frequency change. There is an infinite number of different amplitude and frequency changes.
FSK does make frequency changes for amplitude changes but for only two amplitudes..
Amplitude variations of a HIGH pulse and amplitude variations of a LOW pulse do not effect the amount of frequency change.
Therefore, the amount of frequency variation produced by a HIGH or LOW level is not dependent on the actual level. Only if the signal is HIGH or LOW.
In other words noise, amplitude variations, does not effect a FSK system unless the noise changes a LOW to a HIGH or a HIGH to a LOW.
Last, let's talk about the characteristics of FSK systems..
Since FSK signals are FM signals with only two frequency shifts, the characteristics are a lot less complex than for analog FM signals.
Let's start off with the frequency of the carrier signal.
The carrier frequency must be higher than the information signal frequency for FSK to operate correctly.
If it was not, the information signal could change from HIGH to LOW or LOW to HIGH during the time of one carrier cycle.
This would cause an incorrect frequency shift of the FSK signal.
As a general rule, the carrier frequency must be at least five times the highest information or modulating signal frequency.
This ensures that for each information bit, or data bit, there is around five cycles of the carrier signal frequency, either higher or lower than fc.
The number of cycles for each data bit is important in the demodulator for determining if the signal is HIGH or LOW.
Having less than around five cycles for each data bit, the demodulator would not be able to determine the frequency and could not recover the HIGH or LOW data bit.
What is the minimum carrier frequency in a FSK system that uses information signal up to 10 kHz?

TRY AGAIN!
10 kHz is the highest information signal frequency, fc must be higher.
TRY AGAIN!
MINIMUM fc - The minimum carrier frequency in a FSK system must be at least 5 times the highest information signal frequency.
The second characteristic of FSK signals is Bandwidth......
The bandwidth of a FSK system is always the highest frequency in the FSK signal.
For example, if the bandwidth of a FSK system was set to fc, a modulated carrier signal would contain fmin for LOW information signals and fmax for HIGH information signals.
Since fmax is a higher frequency than fc, the frequency shift for HIGH information would be lost if BW is set to fc.
Also, if the bandwidth of the system was set to fmin (frequency shift for LOW information), the frequencies of fc and fmax (frequency shift of HIGH information) would be lost.
If a FSK system has a carrier signal of 100 kHz and uses 1 kHz frequency changes, what is the bandwidth of the system?
99 kHz is the frequency that represents LOW information signals. Since the system uses two higher frequencies, the bandwidth cannot be set to fmin...
TRY AGAIN!
100 kHz is the carrier frequency that represents no information transmitted. Since the system uses one higher frequency, the bandwidth cannot be set to fc.
TRY AGAIN!
BANDWIDTH - The bandwidth of a FSK system is the highest frequency in the FSK signal.
The last characteristic is noise...........................
As brought out, noise does not effect a FSK system.........
First, amplitude variations in the digital data does not effect the resultant frequency shifts in the FSK signal.
Second, noise picked up in the transmission of the FSK signal can be eliminated by limiters in the demodulator, just like in FM demodulators.
So, is a FSK signal completely free from noise? NO.
The noise that may be in a FSK system is from circuits before and after the FSK modulator and demodulator.
If a A/D and D/A converter is used, quantization noise is added, just like in a PCM system.
Also, if a Delta Modulation system is used, noise is added.
To sum up, noise in a FSK system is not due to the FSK system, but due to other systems that may be required for system operation.
As you have seen, FSK is a simple version of FM that uses digital information signals.
This completes the information on FSK SIGNALS.TITLE........
1. Frequency Shift Keying is a signal processing technique that uses digital signals..
2. The FSK signal is a frequency modulated analog signal that frequency changes indicate HIGHs and LOWs.
3. There are three frequencies in a FSK signal.
fmin - lower frequency to indicate LOWs (or HIGHs)
fc - center frequency to indicate no information signal
fmax - higher frequency to indicate HIGHs (or LOWs)))))))
4. The carrier signal must be at least five times the highest information signal frequency or 5 times the modulating frequency.
5. The bandwidth of a FSK system is the highest frequency in the FSK signal, or fmax.
6. Noise introduced into the FSK signal does not effect the system.
7. The only noise in a FSK system is the noise introduced by other signal processing techniques.

FSK MODULATOR CIRCUITS
FSK modulators normally use integrated circuits............
DISCUSSION
However, FSK has been around a long time and you will find FSK circuits that use vacuum tubes and discrete transistor circuits.
No matter the type of FSK modulator circuit used, they all operate the same.
A FSK modulator has two basic circuits.....................
The switching circuit is used to produce three separate voltages from the digital information signal.
The voltages represent HIGH, LOW and no information inputs to the modulators.
The output of the switching circuit is then applied to a FM modulator circuit.
Many types of switching circuits can be used. A typical switching circuit used in newer FSK systems is in integrated circuit form.
The switch has three connections, IN, OUT, and CONTROL.
With the CONTROL input LOW, the switch is OPEN.
With the CONTROL input HIGH, the switch is CLOSED.
One example of an integrated circuit switch is the MC14066 quad analog transmission gate.
It has four separate switches along with the power and ground connections.
You will see how the switches are used to produce the three voltages in the FSK circuit operation lesson.
What is the output of the FSK modulator's switching circuit?
fmin, fc, and fmax are the FM signals that the entire modulator produces. They are not the output of the switching circuit.
TRY AGAIN!
Digital signals are the input to the FSK modulator. They are not the output of the switching circuit.
TRY AGAIN!
The FM modulator circuit receives the three signals from the switching circuit and generates the FSK signal.
The FM modulator produces fmin for LOW information, fc for no information, and fmax for HIGH information.
Any type of FM modulator will work, reactance -- varactor, VCO, etc.
In newer FSK modulators, integrated circuit VCOs ( Voltage Controlled Oscillators ) are normally used.
VCOs ( Voltage Controlled Osciare normally used.

An example of an IC VCO is the ICL8038. It is similar to the NE566 VCO you studied in the FM lessons.
The advantage to the ICL8038 over the NE566 is that it is more controllable.
Pins 6 and 11 allow for dual power sources. Pin 11 is grounded when one power source is used.
The input to the VCO is applied to pin 8 and is limited to signals between 0.001 and 300 kHz.
The input frequency is limited due to the maximum output frequency of the ICL8038 VCO.
Since 300 kHz is the limit, what is the approximate maximum carrier frequency of the VCO used in FSK systems?
300 kHz is the maximum information signal frequency that can be applied to the input of the VCO. In FSK systems, the carrier signal is always higher.

CARRIER SIGNAL - In FSK systems, the carrier frequency is normally five times the highest information signal.

The center frequency of the chip is determined by the value of a capacitor connected to pin 10.

FSK DEMODULATOR CIRCUITS
FSK demodulators normally use integrated circuits..........
DISCUSSION
And, as in FSK modulators, FSK demodulators can be found constructed from vacuum tube circuits and discrete transistor circuits.
A FSK demodulator has two basic circuits...................
The FM demodulator circuit is used to change the FSK signal to HIGHs and LOWs associated with fmin and fmax.
Many types of FM demodulators can be used such as the slope, discriminator, ratio, phase lock loop (PLL), etc.
In newer FSK demodulators, integrated circuit PLLs are normally used...
In newer FSK demodulators, integrated circuit PLLs are normally used...

PHASE LOCK LOOP (PLL) CIRCUITS - PLL circuits use a phase comparator that compares the FM input signal to the output of a VCO. Any difference in the two signals is sent out of an amplitude level (demodulated FM signal) and used to control the frequency of the VCO.
An example of an IC PLL is the NE565. Yes, it is the same one used in the FM lessons.
Pins 4 and 5 are connected as in any FM demodulator.
But, that's where the similarities end. The chip is configured differently in FSK circuits than in FM circuits.
First, both inputs are used, pins 2 and 3.
Second, both outputs are used, pins 6 and 7.
Also, the FSK demodulator has filters added to the outputs to ensure that the output is HIGH or LOW only.
You will see how the external circuits are connected to the PLL in the FSK circuit operating lesson.
What is the output of the FSK demodulator's FM circuit?
fmin, fc, and fmax are the inputs to the FSK demodulator. They are not the output of the FM demodulator circuit.
TRY AGAIN!
An output of one of three voltage levels is used in the FSK modulator to produce fmin, fc, and fmax.

The fc detector circuit is used to recognize the presence of the carrier signal.
This is very important in FSK demodulators.
Recall that when no information signal is sent, the FSK modulator sends the carrier signal, fc.
When the fc signal is received in the FSK receiver, the signal is demodulated in the FM demodulator circuit.
However, the FM demodulator is designed to demodulate fmin to a LOW and fmax to a HIGH.
fc is demodulated into something, but what? A HIGH or a LOW or something in between?
Whatever the case, it will be incorrect. The output of the demodulator should not be a digital pulse when no information signal is sent.
Using the fc detector circuit, you can tell if the carrier signal was transmitted or not.
If fc was not transmitted, the output of the fc detector circuit is HIGH (or, depending on chip, a LOW).
The HIGH is used to enable the output of the FM demodulator or is used in an indicator (turning the indicator off or on indicating fc was not received).
If fc was transmitted, the output of the fc detector circuit is LOW (or, depending on chip, a HIGH).
The LOW can be used to disable the output of the FM demodulator or used in an indicator (turning the indicator on or off indicating fc was received).
The fc detector circuit is used to indicate that the demodulated output is either information or no information.
Again, a PLL circuit works great for this type of circuit..
In this case, a less complex PLL circuit is used, a NE567 tone decoder IC (VCO remains at a constant frequency).
In this case, a less complex PLL circuit is used, a NE567 tone decoder IC (VCO remains at a constant frequency).
TONE DECODER PLL - The tone decoder uses a set VCO frequency and only outputs a HIGH or LOW, depending on if the input frequency is equal to the VCO frequency or not.
Power is applied to pin 4 and the chip's ground is on pin 7.
The components connected to pins 5 and 6 determine the chip's center frequency or VCO frequency, which is set to fc.
The FM signal input is applied to pin 3 and a HIGH or LOW output is taken from pin 8.
When the FM signal input is the same as the chip's center frequency, a LOW is generated on pin 8 in this chip.
In other words there is no difference between the internal VCO frequency and the FM signal input indicating fc was transmitted, no information.
In other words there is no difference between the internal VCO frequency and the FM signal input indicating fc was transmitted, no information.
PLL CIRCUIT - When the VCO frequency equals the input frequency, the output of the phase comparator is 0. The 0 is sent out from the PLL circuit as a LOW.
When the FM signal input is not the same as the chip's center frequency, a HIGH is generated on pin 8 in this chip.
In other words there is a difference between the internal VCO frequency and the FM signal input indicating that fmin or fmax was transmitted.
In other words there is a difference between the internal VCO frequency and the FM signal input indicating that fmin or fmax was transmitted.

PLL CIRCUIT - When the VCO frequency does not equal the input frequency, the output of the phase comparator is a DC signal.
